triples.rationale: Malachi charges priests with abandoning the way, weakening others through law and corrupting Levi's covenant. Hosea condemns rejection of knowledge and forgetting God's law, linking priestly failure with the people's sins and shared punishment.
triples.source_text: But you have turned aside from the way and weakened many through the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: My people were likened to one without knowledge. Because you thrust away recognition, I too will thrust you away from serving Me as priest. You forgot your God’s law, and I too will forget your children.
According to their multitude, so they sinned against Me; I will turn their glory into dishonor.
They will eat My people’s sins and take their souls amid their injustices.
It will be as with the people, so with the priest; I will exact punishment upon him for his ways and repay him for his schemes.

triples.rationale: Malachi names partiality in the law as a reason for the priests' humiliation. Deuteronomy forbids perverting judgment or showing partiality, supplying a direct legal standard for the conduct Malachi condemns.
triples.source_text: “And I have made you despised and neglected among all the nations, because you did not guard My ways but showed partiality in the law.”

target_units.text: They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.

triples.rationale: Malachi appeals to one Creator and Father as the reason not to abandon a brother and profane the covenant. Deuteronomy likewise challenges an unfaithful people by naming the Lord as the Father who acquired, made and created them.
triples.source_text: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?

target_units.text: Do you thus repay the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? Is not He Himself your Father, who acquired you, and made you, and created you?

triples.rationale: Malachi's appeal to one God and one Father grounds responsibility toward a brother. Ephesians similarly names one God and Father of all within its account of the community's unity.
triples.source_text: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?

target_units.text: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

triples.rationale: Malachi charges Judah with profaning the Lord's holy things and devoting himself to foreign gods. Deuteronomy warns against turning away to other gods and contrasts their worship with Israel's identity as God's holy, chosen people.
triples.source_text: Judah has been abandoned, and an abomination has occurred in Israel and Jerusalem, because Judah profaned the Lord’s holy things, in which he delighted, and devoted himself to foreign gods.

target_units.text: For he will turn your son away from Me, and he will serve other gods; and the Lord shall be kindled to wrath against you, and shall destroy you speedily.
But you shall do thus unto them: you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire.
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, above all the nations upon the face of the earth.

triples.rationale: Malachi threatens removal from Jacob's dwellings after the profanation described in 2:11. Leviticus also announces destruction from among the people for defiling God's holy things; its particular offense of giving offspring to a ruler is distinct from Malachi's wording.
triples.source_text: The Lord will destroy the person who does these things, until he is also humbled away from Jacob’s dwellings and from those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And I will set My face against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he gave some of his seed to a ruler, defiling My holy things and profaning the name of those consecrated to Me.

triples.rationale: Malachi questions accepting sacrifices despite tears and groaning, with abandonment of a spouse identified in the next verse. Isaiah likewise refuses multiplied prayers from people whose hands carry wrongdoing and requires their conduct to change.
triples.source_text: And you were doing these things that I hated: you covered the Lord’s altar with tears, with weeping and groaning from hardships. Is it still fitting to look toward a sacrifice or accept it from your hands?

target_units.text: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.

triples.rationale: Malachi calls the abandoned wife a partner and wife of covenant, with God as witness. Genesis describes the man cleaving to his wife and the two becoming one flesh, grounding the enduring marital bond that abandonment violates.
triples.source_text: And you said, “For what reason?” Because the Lord bore witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you abandoned, though she is your partner and the wife of your covenant.

target_units.text: And Adam said: This, at last, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, for she was taken from her husband.
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.

triples.rationale: The closing command of Malachi 2:15 is to guard one's spirit and not abandon the wife of youth. Paul similarly instructs a husband not to dismiss his wife and a wife not to separate, with reconciliation if separation occurs.
triples.source_text: And no other did it, and there was a remnant of his spirit. And you said, “What else does God seek but offspring?” So guard your spirit, and do not abandon the wife of your youth.

target_units.text: To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband—
but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.

triples.rationale: Malachi links sending a hated wife away with impiety and commands against abandonment. Jesus connects divorce with hardness of heart and warns that divorce followed by remarriage, apart from the stated exception, commits adultery.
triples.source_text: But if, after hating her, you send her away, says the Lord, the God of Israel, impiety will cover your thoughts, says the Lord Almighty. So guard your spirit, and you must not abandon.

target_units.text: He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”

triples.rationale: Malachi condemns saying that evildoers are good before God and questioning His righteousness. Isaiah pronounces woe on calling evil good and on justifying the ungodly while denying the righteous their right, indicting the same reversal of moral judgment.
triples.source_text: You who provoke God with your words! And you said, “How have we provoked Him?” By your saying, “Everyone who does evil is good before the Lord, and He has delighted in them,” and, “Where is the God of righteousness?”

target_units.text: Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, making darkness light and light darkness, making bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are discerning in their own judgment and knowledgeable in their own view!
Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!

triples.rationale: Malachi announces a messenger attending to a way before the Lord's face. Isaiah calls for preparing the Lord's way before His glory and salvation are revealed, supplying a closely related image of preparation for divine arrival.
triples.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low; all the crooked places will become straight, and the rough country will become plains.
And the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God; for the Lord has spoken.

triples.rationale: Jesus identifies John as the prophet about whom the sending of the messenger before the face and preparation of the way was written. The quoted messenger announcement corresponds to Malachi's opening promise, with the quotation's pronouns preserved in Matthew.
triples.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way before Thee.’

triples.rationale: Mark places the messenger-before-the-face announcement beside Isaiah's wilderness voice and then introduces John baptizing. The first announcement corresponds to Malachi's messenger promise, within a combined citation headed by Isaiah in Mark's actual text.
triples.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way;
a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’”
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

triples.rationale: Luke records Jesus identifying John by the written promise of a messenger sent before the face to prepare the way. This repeats Malachi's messenger theme while preserving Luke's wording about preparing the way ahead of the addressed figure.
triples.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way ahead of Thee.’

triples.rationale: Malachi asks who can endure the coming figure's entrance or stand at his appearance. Nahum similarly asks who can stand before the Lord's anger, with melting and crushing imagery emphasizing the overwhelming encounter.
triples.source_text: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

target_units.text: Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.

triples.rationale: Malachi compares the entrant to a smelting fire. Isaiah describes God's hand bringing a people through burning to purity and removing lawlessness, a corresponding image of divine purification rather than mere outward observance.
triples.source_text: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

target_units.text: I will bring My hand against you and burn you to purity. I will destroy the disobedient, remove all lawless people from you and humble all the arrogant.

triples.rationale: Malachi pictures the sons of Levi cleansed like silver and gold so they can offer rightly. Zechariah likewise describes a remnant refined as silver and tested as gold, followed by restored recognition between God and His people.
triples.source_text: He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.

target_units.text: I will lead the third through fire, refine them with fire as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. He will call on My name, and I will listen to him and say, ‘This is My people,’ and he will say, ‘The Lord is my God.’”

triples.rationale: Malachi's refiner succeeds in cleansing the priestly sons for righteous sacrifice. Jeremiah describes a silversmith working in vain because wickedness remains, leading to rejected silver; the shared refining image has contrasting outcomes.
triples.source_text: He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.

target_units.text: The bellows failed from the fire; the lead failed. In vain the silversmith works silver; their wickedness was not melted away.
Call them rejected silver, because the Lord rejected them.

triples.rationale: Malachi promises that Judah and Jerusalem's sacrifice will again please the Lord. The psalm asks for Zion's good and Jerusalem's rebuilding, then anticipates God's delight in a sacrifice of righteousness and offerings on His altar.
triples.source_text: And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old and as in the former years.

target_units.text: Do good to Zion, Lord, in Thy good pleasure, and let Jerusalem’s walls be built.
Then Thou wilt delight in a sacrifice of righteousness, an offering and burnt offerings; then they will bring calves upon Thine altar.

triples.rationale: Malachi's judgment list includes false swearing by God's name and withholding workers' wages. These adjacent Levitical commands prohibit both unjust swearing by God's name and retaining a hired worker's wages overnight.
triples.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.

triples.rationale: Malachi names withheld wages and wrongs against widows, orphans and sojourners. Deuteronomy requires prompt wages for the needy and prohibits perverting judgment for the sojourner, orphan or widow, matching these particular accusations.
triples.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: You shall not withhold the wages of the poor and needy, whether of your brethren or of the sojourners within your cities.
On the same day you shall pay his wages; the sun shall not go down upon them, for he is poor and sets his hope upon them; lest he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be sin upon you.
Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers. Each shall die for his own sin.
You shall not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, or of the orphan, or of the widow; neither shall you take a widow’s garment in pledge.

triples.rationale: Malachi promises swift divine testimony against those withholding a hired worker's pay. James says withheld harvest wages cry out and that the harvesters' cries reach the Lord Sabaoth, likewise placing wage injustice before divine judgment.
triples.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.

triples.rationale: Malachi threatens judgment for harming widows, orphans and sojourners. Exodus prohibits afflicting these groups and says God hears their cries and responds in wrath, supplying the protective principle behind the threatened judgment.
triples.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner, neither shall you afflict him; for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.

triples.rationale: Malachi's opening declaration says the Lord has not changed. The psalm contrasts changing, perishing creation with God who remains the same and whose years do not fail, expressing the same divine constancy.
triples.source_text: “For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed. But you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain

target_units.text: They will perish, but Thou wilt remain; all will grow old like a garment. Like a cloak Thou wilt change them, and they will be changed.
But Thou art the same, and Thy years will not fail.

triples.rationale: Malachi declares that the Lord has not changed. James says the Father of lights has no variation or shadow from turning, applying divine constancy to the source of good gifts.
triples.source_text: “For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed. But you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain

target_units.text: Every good act of giving and every complete gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow from turning.
